entities.summary:
The Master of Business Administration (MBA) is a postgraduate academic degree that originated in the Classical era and has become a global standard for business education. This degree is a direct result of the need for specialized management skills in the empires and foundational civilizations of the time. The MBA is a response to the growing complexity of business organizations and the need for professionals to manage them effectively.

The MBA degree was first introduced in the 19th century in the United States, with the first MBA program established at Harvard Business School in 1908. The degree gained popularity in the mid-20th century, with the establishment of business schools around the world. Today, the MBA is a highly sought-after degree, with thousands of programs offered globally.

The MBA has had a significant impact on the business world, with many graduates going on to become successful entrepreneurs, executives, and leaders in their field. The degree has also led to the development of new business disciplines and the growth of the consulting industry. The MBA has also been criticized for its high cost, long duration, and limited job placement rates.

The MBA has left a lasting legacy in the business world, with many successful companies and leaders having MBAs. The degree has also led to the growth of executive education and the development of new business models and practices.
